title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Field Survey Sheet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Field Survey Sheet
options.lineage: Topographic and cadastral field survey maps
options.thesis: The farm read as one surveyed map sheet: the satellite readings become the map, and the legend explains every term.
materials: map sheet with a title block
options.viewport: A title block banner, a large field-parcel map shaded by soil moisture, and three readings set as map annotations, with the irrigation advice stamped onto the target parcel.
options.risk: Map conventions can read as bureaucratic if the type is timid or the hatching is too fine to see on a projector.

raised.raise: Every reading carries its 7-day trend next to its value, so it can be cross-checked like instruments.
Moisture zones use a hatching pattern as well as colour, so colour is never the only signal.
The advice sits on a day-phase strip (dawn, noon, dusk, night) with 18:00 marked as a labelled cue.
The legend stays fixed and level; everything else on the sheet is explained through it.

options.label: False-Colour Satellite Tile
options.thesis: The field seen from orbit: an NDVI-ramped image tile, with readings as overlays.
options.viewport: A full-width satellite tile of the field, with the three readings as overlay tags and advice in a side panel.
options.risk: Also where most NASA hackathon dashboards land; familiar to judges and easy to forget.

options.label: Night-Flight Six-Pack
options.thesis: Field health as a cockpit panel: the readings are gauges you cross-check.
options.viewport: Six dials in two rows (moisture, NDVI, drought, rain, temperature, evapotranspiration) with a caution lamp that opens the advice.
options.case: Clear to read and shows trends, but a cockpit tells a pilot's story, not a farmer's.
options.risk: Dark cockpit mode fights the requested green/blue nature tone and can feel like a game.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.thesis: The day as horizon bands, from night to dawn to day.
options.viewport: Horizon bands stacked from dark to light, with readings as lighting cues.
options.case: Beautiful, but it hides the field; judges would see stage lighting, not a farm.
options.risk: Farm meaning gets lost in the theatre.

options.label: One-Bit Desktop
options.thesis: Dithered patterns stand in for every tone.
options.case: A retro novelty, and it drops the green/blue brief.
options.risk: Reads as a joke to judges.
options.kept: Pattern as well as tone, so colour is never the only signal.

options.label: Gravity-Rain Garden
options.thesis: Rain falls according to each cloud's own gravity.
options.case: Whimsical; hides the numbers and the advice.
options.kept: A fixed, level legend that everything else is read through.

options.label: Copy-Shop Zine
options.thesis: One typed column on coloured copier paper.
options.viewport: A single typed column of readings.
options.case: Punk register, wrong for a science demo.
options.kept: A strict one-column measure for the advice text.

options.label: Leather Studio
options.thesis: Digital things as loved physical objects.
options.viewport: Readings on a stitched leather shelf.
options.case: Nostalgic app chrome; no connection to farms or satellites.
options.kept: Every section is an object you handle.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean agri-tech SaaS dashboard: cards, badges and charts, done at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A header, three KPI cards, a chart row and an advice button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other hackathon dashboard, by design.
